# The element / component vocabulary

<!-- generated from packages/vocabulary/data/vocabulary.json by scripts/vocabulary-docs.mjs: do not edit -->

Generated by `npm run vocabulary:docs` (scripts/vocabulary-docs.mjs) from `packages/vocabulary/data/vocabulary.json` and
`maps.json`. One term per thing, in four namespaces, each with an ordered identification rule set that a script runs
(`identify()` in JS, `vocabulary_rules.py` for the slide-anatomy skill), never a judgment. When no rule decides, the
answer is `unknown` - returned, never a guess, and counted. Plan: docs/PLAN-template-library.md §1.

| namespace | question | terms |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | primitive: what is drawn | 7 |
| E2 | role: what a thing is for on the slide | 56 |
| E3 | structure: what things form together | 46 |
| E4 | treatment: how a thing is finished | 38 |

## How a term is identified: the chains

A chain is one question asked of one kind of subject. Its rules run in order; each rule runs over every subject still
unassigned, and the first rule that holds decides (so "the largest free text" is the largest text no earlier rule took).

### Chain `element` (E2)

Subject: an object on a slide (anatomy L1 object, catalogue header part or field, deck element). What an object is for on the slide. Block-aware rules (a field of a marked block: catalogue, our own decks) run first, then the text wording rules, then the geometry rules for text, then the rules for marks, images and shapes.

### Chain `block` (E3)

Subject: a marked container (catalogue `containers[]`, a content/2 block) with the E2 terms of its fields. Which content/2 block type a container is, from its item structure and the roles of its fields.

None: when fields = 0 - holds no field of its own: nothing to identify (the title container).

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | `table-block.cells` | [table-block](#e3-table-block) | termCount.cell > 0 | its fields are rows of cells |
| 20 | `kpis.figures` | [kpis](#e3-kpis) | itemShare.big-number >= 0.5 | half of its items or more hold a big-number |
| 30 | `chart-block.labels` | [chart-block](#e3-chart-block) | termShare.label = 1 | every field is a short label over a drawn area |
| 40 | `paragraph-block.text` | [paragraph-block](#e3-paragraph-block) | termShare.paragraph = 1 | its one field is a paragraph |
| 50 | `points.bullets` | [points](#e3-points) | termShare.bullet = 1 | every field is a bullet |
| 55 | `quotes.marks` | [quotes](#e3-quotes) | itemShare.quote >= 0.5 | half of its items or more open with a quote mark |
| 56 | `people.avatars` | [people](#e3-people) | itemShare.avatar >= 0.5 | half of its items or more hold an avatar |
| 57 | `logos.marks` | [logos](#e3-logos) | termCount.logo-item >= 3 | three logo items or more |
| 58 | `image-block.only` | [image-block](#e3-image-block) | imageOnly | it holds images only |
| 59 | `compare.contrast` | [compare](#e3-compare) | minItemFields >= 2; items = 2; labelText matches `contrast` | two items, the first labelled as one side of a contrast (From, Then, Before ...) |
| 60 | `timeline.periods` | [timeline](#e3-timeline) | minItemFields >= 2; (labelText matches `period`) or (headText matches `periodStart`) | its items are labelled by dates / periods (2024, Q1 2026, Feb 2025, Now) |
| 65 | `process.ordinals` | [process](#e3-process) | minItemFields >= 2; labelText matches `ordinal` | its items are labelled by step ordinals |
| 70 | `subpoints.lists` | [subpoints](#e3-subpoints) | minItemFields >= 2; listItemShare >= 0.5 | half of its items or more explain their heading with two runs or more |
| 80 | `compare.two-sides` | [compare](#e3-compare) | minItemFields >= 2; items = 2; itemsInRow; between; not numbered | exactly two items side by side with a rule between them, not numbered |
| 85 | `process.connector` | [process](#e3-process) | minItemFields >= 2; (items >= 2 and connector.crossing >= items) or (connector.inner > 0); labelText | a connector line joins every item (one line crosses each of them) or runs through them in pieces, and the first item carries a label: a sequence. Period labels were already decided as timeline (timeline.periods), ordinals as process (process.ordinals); a sequence with any other label (01, a region) is a process. A frame rule over an unlabelled row (a comparison, a column list) is not a connector: the label is required (V1, the answer key: without it 3 lists and 3 column lists turn process) |
| 90 | `items.heading-description` | [items](#e3-items) | minItemFields >= 2; items >= 1 | every item holds two texts or more (a heading and its description) |

| 4 | `radial-gradient.fill` | [radial-gradient](#e4-radial-gradient) | paint = "radial" | painted as radial |
| 5 | `conic-gradient.fill` | [conic-gradient](#e4-conic-gradient) | paint = "conic" | painted as conic |
| 6 | `mesh-gradient.fill` | [mesh-gradient](#e4-mesh-gradient) | paint = "mesh" | painted as mesh |
| 7 | `gradient.fill` | [gradient](#e4-gradient) | paint = "gradient" | painted as gradient |
| 8 | `pattern.fill` | [pattern](#e4-pattern) | paint = "pattern" | painted as pattern |
| 9 | `texture.fill` | [texture](#e4-texture) | paint = "texture" | painted as texture |
| 10 | `image-fill.fill` | [image-fill](#e4-image-fill) | paint = "image" | painted as image |
| 11 | `video.fill` | [video](#e4-video) | paint = "video" | painted as video |

### Chain `emphasis` (E4)

Subject: a run inside a text. How a run is set apart from the rest of its text.

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `face-run.emphasis` | [face-run](#e4-face-run) | faceDiffers | another face |
| 2 | `weight-run.emphasis` | [weight-run](#e4-weight-run) | weightDelta > 0 | another weight |
| 3 | `colour-run.emphasis` | [colour-run](#e4-colour-run) | colourDiffers | another colour |

### Chain `angle` (E4)

Subject: a shape. Whether a shape is cut on a slant.

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `angle.angle` | [angle](#e4-angle) | angles | a non-axis edge |

### Chain `layer` (E4)

Subject: an element that overlaps text. Which side of the text an element is drawn on.

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `behind.layer` | [behind](#e4-behind) | behindText | under the text it overlaps |
| 2 | `front.layer` | [front](#e4-front) | overText | over the text it overlaps |

### Chain `bleed` (E4)

Subject: an element at the slide edge. Whether an element runs off the slide.

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bleed.bleed` | [bleed](#e4-bleed) | bleedCount >= 1 | touches / crosses a slide edge |

### Chain `blend` (E4)

Subject: an element or gradient with a blend mode. Whether an element mixes with what is under it.

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `blend.blend` | [blend](#e4-blend) | blend; not (blend = "normal") | a blend mode other than normal |

### Chain `case` (E4)

Subject: a text. Whether a text is set in a case transform.

| order | rule | term | when | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `case.case` | [case](#e4-case) | (caps) or (caseTransform) | a case transform |

## The predicate set

A rule is `{id, order, when: [predicate, ...], why}`; every predicate must hold. A predicate is an object with one key.
Geometry is in % of the slide (`bbox` = [x0, y0, x1, y1]); `sizePctH` is the text size in % of the slide height.

| predicate | argument | holds when |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `[kinds]` | The subject kind is one of the list (text, image, shape, vectorgroup, region, line, group, chart, table, block, slide, structure, fill, ...). |
| `has` | `field` | The field is set and not false / 0 / empty. |
| `lacks` | `field` | The field is unset, false, 0 or empty. |
| `eq` | `[field, value]` | The field equals the value. |
| `in` | `[field, [values]]` | The field is one of the values. |
| `gte` | `[field, value | {ctx|field, times}, missing?]` | field >= value. |
| `gt` | `[field, value | {ctx|field, times}, missing?]` | field > value. |
| `lte` | `[field, value | {ctx|field, times}, missing?]` | field <= value. |
| `lt` | `[field, value | {ctx|field, times}, missing?]` | field < value. |
| `near` | `[field, value | {ctx|field, times}, tolerance]` | \|field - value\| < tolerance (a missing right side fails). |
| `text` | `pattern name` | The subject's trimmed text matches the named pattern (vocabulary.json `patterns`). |
| `notText` | `pattern name` | The subject has no text, or its trimmed text does not match the named pattern. |
| `match` | `[field, pattern name]` | The named text field of the subject (e.g. a block's `labelText`) matches the named pattern. |
| `any` | `[[predicates], [predicates], ...]` | At least one of the predicate lists holds as a whole (OR of ANDs). |
| `not` | `predicate` | The predicate does not hold. |
| `rank` | `{by, among: {kind, minWords}, tol, tie: "top"}` | The subject is the one with the largest `by` among the subjects unassigned when the rule began that match `among` (a tie within `tol` goes to the topmost): one winner per pass. |
| `stacked` | `{on: term, side: "below" | "above", gapTimesSize, edgeTol, centreTol, grow: [terms]}` | The subject sits directly below / above the subject assigned `on` (the first), on its left edge (within `edgeTol` % W) or centred alike when that one is centred (within `centreTol`), at a gap under `gapTimesSize` x its text size, and is smaller than it. With `grow`, the reference box below grows by each subject already assigned one of those terms (a subtitle stack). |
| `nextTo` | `{rule, below: {dy, dx}, right: {dx, dy}}` | A subject the named rule identified lies just above-left of this one (this one's top within `below.dy` of its bottom, left edges within `below.dx`) or just left of it (this one's left within `right.dx` of its right edge, tops within `right.dy`). |
| `below` | `{kind: [kinds], minArea, gap, overlap}` | The subject sits directly under a subject of one of `kind` covering at least `minArea` % of the slide: its top within `gap` % H under that bottom, overlapping it horizontally by at least `overlap` x its own width. |
| `belowText` | `{pattern, gap, smaller}` | The subject sits directly under a text matching the named pattern: its top within `gap` % H under that bottom, overlapping it horizontally (with `smaller`, set smaller than it). |
| `sibling` | `term` | Another field of the same item (same block and item index) has been assigned the term. |
| `siblingBefore` | `term` | A field of the same item that reads before this one (above it, or left of it on the same row) has been assigned the term. |
| `leads` | `true` | The subject leads its item: of the item's texts unassigned when the rule began (it and at least one other) it has the heaviest weight, and on equal weight it reads first (above, or left on the same row). One leader per item. |

Derived fields (computed by `prepare()` when the measurement does not give them): `words`, `commas`, `hasDigit`,
`capitalShare` (share of words starting upper-case), `x0` `y0` `x1` `y1` `w` `h`, `areaPct`, `aspect` (w / h in slide
units), `inCorner` (top / bottom 22 % and left / right 30 %), `thin` (h < 0.8 % H or w < 0.5 % W), `length` (the longer
side), `spansSide` (w > 95 and h <= 30, or h > 95 and w <= 40), `bleedCount`, `holdsText` / `heldTexts` (non-furniture)
/ `heldWords` / `heldText` (texts inside a non-text box), `sidesWithContent` (0-2: content along a thin line on each side,
the line at least half as long as the wider side), `inBlock`, `itemFields`, `blockItems`. Measured fields a rule may
read: `furniture` (repeated at the same spot on >= 40 % of the deck's pages), `pieces`, `transparent`, `angles`,
`opacity`, `tilt`, `mask`, `pill`, `onEdge`, `pointer`, `stroke`, `fill`, `framesContent`, `itemHead`, `joinsItems`,
`peerMarks`, `numberLabelsInside`, `textsInside`, `series`, `rowPeers`, `activePeer`, `cells`, `subTexts`,
`blockCover`, `blockDataLabels`, and the brand context `inLogos` (true / false: its file is / is not a brand logo), `named`
(the brand names it as its device), `signature` (the L4 signature of a reference record).

## E1 - primitive: what is drawn

<a id="e1-line"></a>
### line

A straight stroke between two points (deck `line`), or a drawn shape so thin it reads as one.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `line.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 1): kind is line. Why: drawn as a line.
- `line.thin-shape` (chain `primitive`, order 2): kind is shape / region; thin. Why: a shape under 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick reads as a line.

Signal: deck element type `line`; a shape under 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick.

Not to be confused with:
- [shape](#e1-shape): a shape has an area; a line has a length only (thin)

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: line`, `deck.shape.kind: line`
- layout: `layout.box.shape.kind: line`
- brand: `brand.template.region.kind: line`
- template: `template.element.primitive: line`

Examples: yes - a 1 px hairline under a header; no - a 40 x 40 px square.

<a id="e1-text"></a>
### text

Glyphs set from a string in a face at a size.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `text.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 11): kind is text. Why: drawn as text.

Signal: deck element type `text`; a text run in a PDF / HTML.

Not to be confused with:
- [image](#e1-image): a word baked into a picture is an image (a logo set as pixels)

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: text`
- template: `template.element.primitive: text`

Examples: yes - a title; no - a logo image of a word.

<a id="e1-image"></a>
### image

A raster or vector picture placed from a file.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `image.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 12): kind is image. Why: drawn as image.

Signal: deck element type `image`; an image XObject / <img>.

Not to be confused with:
- [shape](#e1-shape): a shape is drawn from geometry, an image comes from a file
- [text](#e1-text): a word baked into a picture is an image (a logo set as pixels)

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: image`
- template: `template.element.primitive: image`

Examples: yes - a photo; no - a filled rectangle.

<a id="e1-shape"></a>
### shape

A filled or stroked geometry (rect, ellipse, polygon, path) with an area.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `shape.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 13): kind is shape / region; not thin. Why: drawn as shape / region.

Signal: deck element type `shape`; a vector path; a colour region of a screenshot.

Not to be confused with:
- [line](#e1-line): a line is thin (under 0.8 % H / 0.5 % W)
- [image](#e1-image): an image comes from a file
- [group](#e1-group): a shape is one geometry

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: shape`
- layout: `layout.box.role: shape`
- template: `template.element.primitive: shape`

Examples: yes - a card background; no - a hairline.

<a id="e1-chart"></a>
### chart

A data chart drawn by the renderer from series (deck `chart`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `chart.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 14): kind is chart. Why: drawn as chart.

Signal: deck element type `chart`.

Not to be confused with:
- [group](#e1-group): a group of shapes that only looks like a chart is a group until identified as E2 chart

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: chart`
- template: `template.element.primitive: chart`

Examples: yes - a bar chart element; no - a picture of a chart.

<a id="e1-table"></a>
### table

A grid of cells drawn by the renderer (deck `table`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `table.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 15): kind is table. Why: drawn as table.

Signal: deck element type `table`.

Not to be confused with:
- [group](#e1-group): a table is cells with a row / column model

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: table`
- template: `template.element.primitive: table`

Examples: yes - a 3 x 4 table element; no - three text boxes in a row.

<a id="e1-group"></a>
### group

Several drawn things moved and scaled as one (deck `group`, a PDF vector group).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `group.kind` (chain `primitive`, order 16): kind is group / vectorgroup. Why: drawn as group / vectorgroup.

Signal: deck element type `group`; a vector group of a PDF.

Not to be confused with:
- [shape](#e1-shape): a shape is one geometry
- [chart](#e1-chart): a group of shapes that only looks like a chart is a group until identified as E2 chart
- [table](#e1-table): a table is cells with a row / column model

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.element.type: group`
- layout: `layout.box.role: group`
- template: `template.element.primitive: group`

Examples: yes - a logo drawn as 12 paths; no - one rectangle.

## E2 - role: what a thing is for on the slide

<a id="e2-big-number"></a>
### big-number

A figure set large: a number pattern (26 %, $4.1bn, 3x, 1 in 6, 659 deals) at 1.5 x the body size or more. The stat / KPI value / number of the other vocabularies.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `big-number.block` (chain `element`, order 60): kind is text; inBlock; text matches `number`; text does not match `date`; sizePctH >= 1.5 x bodyPctH. Why: a number pattern (not a year / date) at >= 1.5x body in a block (a KPI value).
- `big-number.size` (chain `element`, order 210): kind is text; text matches `number`; sizePctH >= 1.5 x bodyPctH. Why: a number at >= 1.5x body size.

Signal: text matching `number`, size >= 1.5 x body.

Not to be confused with:
- [heading](#e2-heading): a heading is words; a big-number is a number pattern (a figure word like "Elevenfold" is a number, "No findings" is not)
- [label](#e2-label): a label is smaller than body; a big-number is >= 1.5x body
- [date](#e2-date): a lone year is a date (wording rules run first)
- [page-number](#e2-page-number): a big-number is >= 1.5x body
- [decor-word](#e2-decor-word): a big-number is read as a figure at full strength
- [title](#e2-title): a large figure is a big-number

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: number`, `layout.slot.type: number`
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: stat`, `brand.template.slot.type: stat`, `brand.components: number`
- content: `content.cell.type: number`
- anatomy: `role: big-number`
- catalogue: `data-f: value`
- template: `template.element.role: big-number`, `template.emphasis.carrier: numeral`

Examples: yes - "$504B" at 200 px over 30 px descriptions; no - "2 key findings" at title size (a heading).

<a id="e2-label"></a>
### label

A short text (6 words or fewer) smaller than body that names the thing beside it: a year on a timeline, a process node label, a KPI label, a chart data label, a partner label ("Prepared for").

Identified when (in chain order):
- `label.chart` (chain `element`, order 70): kind is text; inBlock; itemFields = 1; words <= 6; blockDataLabels >= 2. Why: a short one-field item of a block that also shows two figures or more of its own (data labels, not a 1..n numbering): a chart / diagram label.
- `label.partner` (chain `element`, order 150): kind is text; text matches `partner`. Why: 'prepared for / commissioned by' wording: names the partner mark beside it.
- `label.small` (chain `element`, order 340): kind is text; sizePctH < bodyPctH; words <= 6. Why: short and smaller than body.

Signal: words <= 6, size < body; in a block: a one-field item of a block showing >= 2 data labels of its own; partner wording.

Not to be confused with:
- [eyebrow](#e2-eyebrow): an eyebrow sits directly above the title on its edge; a label names the thing beside it
- [caption](#e2-caption): a caption sits under an image; a label names a data point, a node or a partner
- [bullet](#e2-bullet): a bullet is a line of a list that shows no figures of its own; a chart label is an item of a block that shows data labels
- [big-number](#e2-big-number): a label is smaller than body; a big-number is >= 1.5x body
- [date](#e2-date): a year on a timeline or under a chart bar is a label (block rules run first)
- [unknown](#e2-unknown): a label is 6 words or fewer
- [tabs](#e2-tabs): labels name things, nothing is active

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: meta`, `brand.cardBlock.type: footer`
- anatomy: `role: label`, `role: partner-label`
- catalogue: `data-f: point`
- template: `template.element.role: label`

Examples: yes - "2024" under a bar of a column chart; no - a two-line description in a card.

<a id="e2-bullet"></a>
### bullet

One line of a list: an item of a block that holds a single text (with a marker, an indent or a rule between the lines).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `bullet.list-line` (chain `element`, order 80): kind is text; inBlock; itemFields = 1; blockItems >= 1. Why: the only text of its item in a list block.

Signal: a block field alone in its item, the block holding items.

Not to be confused with:
- [description](#e2-description): a description follows a heading in its item; a bullet is alone in its item
- [paragraph](#e2-paragraph): a paragraph is the whole block (no item); a bullet is one item of several
- [label](#e2-label): a chart label is an item of a block that shows data labels
- [attribution](#e2-attribution): a dash bullet ("– faster growth") is not under a quote

Maps from:
- catalogue: `data-f: bullet`
- template: `template.element.role: bullet`

Examples: yes - "Publish rates, fees and terms" in a ticked list; no - the description under a card heading.

<a id="e2-heading"></a>
### heading

The leading text of an item (its name, above or left of what it explains), or on a reference a text larger than body that is not the title.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `heading.item` (chain `element`, order 90): kind is text; inBlock; it leads its item (heaviest, then first). Why: leads its item: the heaviest of the item's free texts (the first in reading order on equal weight).
- `heading.larger` (chain `element`, order 350): kind is text; sizePctH > bodyPctH. Why: larger than body, not the title.

Signal: a block field that leads its item (heaviest weight, then reading order); size > body outside blocks.

Not to be confused with:
- [big-number](#e2-big-number): a big-number is a number pattern at >= 1.5x body
- [title](#e2-title): the title is the largest free text of the slide
- [eyebrow](#e2-eyebrow): an eyebrow is a short line above the title

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: title`
- content: `content.cell.type: heading`
- anatomy: `role: heading`
- catalogue: `data-f: heading`
- template: `template.element.role: heading`

Examples: yes - "Answers, not links" over its description in a card; no - the description under it.

<a id="e2-body"></a>
### body

Running text at the body size (the size carrying the most words once the largest size is left out); in a KPI item, the text explaining the figure.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `body.kpi` (chain `element`, order 95): kind is text; inBlock; a field of its item is big-number. Why: the text of an item that holds a big-number: it explains the figure.
- `body.size` (chain `element`, order 330): kind is text; |sizePctH - bodyPctH| < 0.15. Why: at the body size.

Signal: size within 0.15 % H of the body size; a KPI item field after its figure.

Not to be confused with:
- [description](#e2-description): a description follows a heading in an item without a figure; body explains a figure (KPI) or is free running text
- [paragraph](#e2-paragraph): a paragraph is a block of its own
- [placeholder](#e2-placeholder): real copy
- [contact](#e2-contact): a sentence that mentions a contact centre in running text over 25 words
- [authors](#e2-authors): a sentence with commas in lower case
- [quote-mark](#e2-quote-mark): a quote with its words
- [subtitle](#e2-subtitle): body is not on the title stack

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: body`, `layout.slot.type: text`
- brand: `brand.template.slot.type: body`
- content: `content.cell.type: text`
- anatomy: `role: body`
- catalogue: `data-f: body`
- template: `template.element.role: body`

Examples: yes - "Fintech revenue in 2025 passed half a trillion" under "$504B"; no - a heading.

<a id="e2-description"></a>
### description

Body-size text under (or right of) a heading inside one item: what the heading means.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `description.under-heading` (chain `element`, order 96): kind is text; inBlock; a field before it in its item is heading. Why: reads after the heading of its item.

Signal: a block field read after a field identified as heading in its item.

Not to be confused with:
- [body](#e2-body): body explains a figure; a description explains a heading
- [paragraph](#e2-paragraph): a paragraph has no heading sibling in its item
- [bullet](#e2-bullet): a bullet is alone in its item

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: body`
- catalogue: `data-f: description`
- template: `template.element.role: description`

Examples: yes - the two lines under a card heading; no - a lone paragraph block.

<a id="e2-paragraph"></a>
### paragraph

Running text that is a block of its own (no item), or of 2 lines or more with no heading sibling in its item.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `paragraph.block` (chain `element`, order 97): kind is text; inBlock; not item; itemFields = 1. Why: the block's only run of text, outside any item (one line counts: a one-sentence statement block).
- `paragraph.lines` (chain `element`, order 98): kind is text; inBlock; lines >= 2; not (a field before it in its item is heading). Why: running text of 2 lines or more with no heading in its item.

Signal: a block field without an item index; lines >= 2 with no heading in its item.

Not to be confused with:
- [description](#e2-description): a description follows a heading
- [body](#e2-body): body is a size; paragraph is a block
- [bullet](#e2-bullet): a paragraph is the whole block (no item); a bullet is one item of several

Maps from:
- catalogue: `data-f: paragraph`
- template: `template.element.role: paragraph`

Examples: yes - a 3-line takeaway beside a chart; no - a description under a heading.

<a id="e2-legal"></a>
### legal

Legal wording (copyright, confidentiality, disclaimer) at body size or smaller.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `legal.wording` (chain `element`, order 100): kind is text; text matches `legal`; sizePctH <= 1.05 x bodyPctH (holds when the right side is missing). Why: legal wording at body size or smaller (wording decides before repetition: a repeated copyright line is still legal).

Signal: text matching `legal`, size <= 1.05 x body.

Not to be confused with:
- [footer-text](#e2-footer-text): footer text is repeated furniture without legal wording
- [source](#e2-source): a source cites data

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: legal`
- template: `template.element.role: legal`

Examples: yes - "Copyright © 2025 Example Co. All rights reserved."; no - "Confidential" set as a 40 pt title.

<a id="e2-source"></a>
### source

The line citing where data comes from ("Source: ...", "Note: ...", "n = 1,000").

Identified when (in chain order):
- `source.wording` (chain `element`, order 110): kind is text; text matches `source`; sizePctH <= bodyPctH (holds when the right side is missing). Why: starts with Source / Note, no larger than body (wording decides before repetition).

Signal: text matching `source`, size <= body.

Not to be confused with:
- [footer-text](#e2-footer-text): a footer repeats without citing
- [caption](#e2-caption): a caption describes an image
- [legal](#e2-legal): a source cites data

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: source`
- catalogue: `header: .src`
- template: `template.element.role: source`, `template.mark.part: src`

Examples: yes - "Source: Global Fintech Report 2026"; no - "Sources of growth" as a heading.

<a id="e2-page-number"></a>
### page-number

The slide number: digits only (or "page 3 / 20"), repeated as furniture or in the top / bottom band, no larger than body.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `page-number.furniture` (chain `element`, order 120): kind is text; furniture; text matches `pagenum`. Why: digits only, repeated on >= 40 % of the pages at this spot.
- `page-number.band` (chain `element`, order 140): kind is text; text matches `pagenum`; (y0 > 88) or (y1 < 10); sizePctH <= bodyPctH (holds when the right side is missing). Why: digits only, in the top / bottom band, not larger than body.

Signal: text matching `pagenum`, furniture or in the top / bottom 10 % band.

Not to be confused with:
- [big-number](#e2-big-number): a big-number is >= 1.5x body
- [footer-text](#e2-footer-text): footer text holds words
- [pager](#e2-pager): a page number is one number

Maps from:
- brand: `mood.footer.items: pageNumber`
- anatomy: `role: page-number`
- template: `template.element.role: page-number`

Examples: yes - "12" bottom right on every page; no - "12%" at 80 pt.

<a id="e2-footer-text"></a>
### footer-text

Text repeated at the same spot on 40 % or more of a deck's pages (the deck's furniture): brand name, deck title, running head.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `footer-text.furniture` (chain `element`, order 130): kind is text; furniture. Why: repeated on >= 40 % of the deck's pages at this spot.

Signal: furniture (deck signature repeated on >= 40 % of pages; digits count as one sign).

Not to be confused with:
- [page-number](#e2-page-number): digits only
- [legal](#e2-legal): legal wording
- [source](#e2-source): source wording

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: footer`
- brand: `mood.footer.items: text`, `brand.template.slot.type: footer`
- anatomy: `role: footer`
- catalogue: `header: .ft`
- template: `template.element.role: footer-text`, `template.mark.part: ft`

Examples: yes - "ACME 7" (a caps brand word + the page number) at the bottom left of every slide; no - a subtitle.

<a id="e2-date"></a>
### date

A whole-line date (month year, Q1 2024, 7 July 2020, a lone year).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `date.pattern` (chain `element`, order 160): kind is text; text matches `date`. Why: date pattern.

Signal: text matching `date`.

Not to be confused with:
- [label](#e2-label): a year on a timeline or under a chart bar is a label (block rules run first)
- [big-number](#e2-big-number): a lone year is a date even when large

Maps from:
- brand: `mood.footer.items: date`
- anatomy: `role: date`
- template: `template.element.role: date`

Examples: yes - "January 2024" under a cover title; no - "In 2024 revenue doubled".

<a id="e2-placeholder"></a>
### placeholder

Template filler left in place ("Lorem ipsum", "Click to add", "XX", "Partner logo"). A QA finding.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `placeholder.wording` (chain `element`, order 170): kind is text; text matches `placeholder`. Why: placeholder wording (QA).

Signal: text matching `placeholder`.

Not to be confused with:
- [body](#e2-body): real copy

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: placeholder`
- template: `template.element.role: placeholder`

Examples: yes - "Click to add title"; no - "Add value to every client".

<a id="e2-contact"></a>
### contact

Contact details or a closing line: email, web address, phone, "thank you", "get in touch" (25 words or fewer).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `contact.wording` (chain `element`, order 180): kind is text; text matches `contact`; words <= 25. Why: email / web / phone / thank-you wording.

Signal: text matching `contact`, words <= 25.

Not to be confused with:
- [body](#e2-body): a sentence that mentions a contact centre in running text over 25 words

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: contact`
- template: `template.element.role: contact`

Examples: yes - "hello@brand.com"; no - a 40-word paragraph about contact centres.

<a id="e2-authors"></a>
### authors

A list of names: 2 or more commas, no digits, at least 70 % of the words capitalised, 60 words or fewer.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `authors.names` (chain `element`, order 190): kind is text; commas >= 2; not hasDigit; words <= 60; capitalShare >= 0.7. Why: comma-separated capitalised names, no digits.

Signal: commas >= 2, no digit, capitalShare >= 0.7.

Not to be confused with:
- [body](#e2-body): a sentence with commas in lower case
- [attribution](#e2-attribution): authors list names with commas

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: authors`
- template: `template.element.role: authors`

Examples: yes - "Ana Lima, Ben Okafor, Chen Wei"; no - "Fast, cheap, and good enough".

<a id="e2-quote-mark"></a>
### quote-mark

A quotation glyph set on its own (a large “ as decoration of a quote).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `quote-mark.glyph` (chain `element`, order 195): kind is text; text matches `quoteGlyph`. Why: only quote glyphs.

Signal: text of quote glyphs only.

Not to be confused with:
- [decor](#e2-decor): a drawn quote shape is decor unless named
- [body](#e2-body): a quote with its words

Maps from:
- template: `template.element.role: quote-mark`

Examples: yes - "“" at 200 pt; no - "“Great product”".

<a id="e2-attribution"></a>
### attribution

Who said a quote: a line of 15 words or fewer, smaller than the quote, directly under its closing line ("— Jane Doe, CEO").

Identified when (in chain order):
- `attribution.under-quote` (chain `element`, order 196): kind is text; words <= 15; directly under a text matching `quoteEnd` (gap <= 4 % H, smaller than it). Why: directly under the end of a quote (a text closing with a quote mark), smaller than it, 15 words or fewer.

Signal: under a smaller text ending with a closing quote mark (gap <= 4 % H).

Not to be confused with:
- [caption](#e2-caption): a caption describes an image
- [authors](#e2-authors): authors list names with commas
- [bullet](#e2-bullet): a dash bullet ("– faster growth") is not under a quote

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: attribution`
- template: `template.element.role: attribution`

Examples: yes - "— Jane Doe, CEO" under “We moved faster”; no - "– faster growth" in a dash list.

<a id="e2-caption"></a>
### caption

A short phrase directly under an image that says what it shows (2 to 30 words, smaller than body, not a figure).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `caption.under-image` (chain `element`, order 197): kind is text; sizePctH < bodyPctH (holds when the right side is missing); words >= 2; words <= 30; text does not match `number`; directly under a image of >= 1.5 % (gap <= 2 % H). Why: a phrase directly under a picture (within 2 % H), smaller than body, not a figure.

Signal: text whose top is within 2 % H under an image of >= 1.5 % of the slide, overlapping it by half its width, smaller than body.

Not to be confused with:
- [label](#e2-label): a label names a data point / node / partner
- [source](#e2-source): a source cites data
- [eyebrow](#e2-eyebrow): an eyebrow sits above the title
- [attribution](#e2-attribution): a caption describes an image

Maps from:
- template: `template.element.role: caption`

Examples: yes - "Our Berlin office" under a photo; no - a title over a photo.

<a id="e2-decor-word"></a>
### decor-word

A word set as decoration (a giant faded "2024", a background word): 3 words or fewer at half opacity or less.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `decor-word.faded` (chain `element`, order 98.5): kind is text; words <= 3; opacity <= 0.5. Why: a word or two at half opacity or less: decoration, not copy.

Signal: text, words <= 3, opacity <= 0.5.

Not to be confused with:
- [big-number](#e2-big-number): a big-number is read as a figure at full strength
- [watermark](#e2-watermark): a watermark is an image / mark

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: word`
- template: `template.element.role: decor-word`

Examples: yes - "GROW" at 400 pt, 10 % opacity, behind the title; no - the title.

<a id="e2-title"></a>
### title

The largest free text of the slide (the topmost one on a tie).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `title.largest` (chain `element`, order 300): kind is text; the largest sizePctH among the free text (topmost within 0.05). Why: largest free text (topmost on a tie).

Signal: largest size among texts no earlier rule took.

Not to be confused with:
- [heading](#e2-heading): a heading leads an item or is a smaller free text
- [big-number](#e2-big-number): a large figure is a big-number

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: title`
- brand: `brand.template.slot.type: title`
- content: `content.v1.block.type: title`
- anatomy: `role: title`
- catalogue: `header: .t`
- template: `template.element.role: title`, `template.mark.part: t`

Examples: yes - the 56 px headline of a slide; no - a 200 px KPI value.

<a id="e2-subtitle"></a>
### subtitle

A text directly under the title (gap under 1.6 x the title size), on its edge (or centred alike), smaller than the title, at body size or larger.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `subtitle.under-title` (chain `element`, order 310): kind is text; words >= 1; directly below the title (gap < 1.6 x its size, same edge, the subtitle stack growing); sizePctH >= 0.95 x bodyPctH (holds when the right side is missing). Why: directly under the title, same edge, smaller.

Signal: stacked below the title stack.

Not to be confused with:
- [eyebrow](#e2-eyebrow): an eyebrow is above the title
- [body](#e2-body): body is not on the title stack

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: subtitle`
- brand: `brand.template.slot.type: subtitle`
- content: `content.v1.block.type: subtitle`
- anatomy: `role: subtitle`
- template: `template.element.role: subtitle`

Examples: yes - "Key Insights Report" under a cover title; no - a source line at the bottom.

<a id="e2-eyebrow"></a>
### eyebrow

A short line (8 words or fewer) directly above the title, on its edge (the kicker).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `eyebrow.above-title` (chain `element`, order 320): kind is text; words >= 1; directly above the title (gap < 1.6 x its size, same edge); words <= 8. Why: short line just above the title, same edge.

Signal: stacked above the title, words <= 8.

Not to be confused with:
- [label](#e2-label): a label names the thing beside it
- [caption](#e2-caption): a caption is under an image
- [subtitle](#e2-subtitle): a subtitle is under the title
- [heading](#e2-heading): an eyebrow is a short line above the title

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: eyebrow`
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: eyebrow`
- content: `content.v1.block.type: eyebrow`
- anatomy: `role: eyebrow`
- catalogue: `header: .k`
- template: `template.element.role: eyebrow`, `template.mark.part: k`

Examples: yes - "SEARCH TO ANSWERS" over the title; no - the date under the title.

<a id="e2-unknown"></a>
### unknown

What no rule decides. Returned, never a guess; counted, so the vocabulary measures its own gaps. On a reference, the old anatomy role small-text (smaller than body, more than 6 words) is unknown: no test says what it is.

Identified when: no rule holds (it is the answer of no rule).

Signal: no rule of the chain holds.

Not to be confused with:
- [label](#e2-label): a label is 6 words or fewer

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.imagery.sample.kind: unknown`, `brand.template.slot.type: custom`
- anatomy: `role: small-text`
- template: `template.element.role: unknown`, `template.category: unknown`

Examples: yes - a 12-word line at 80 % of body size with nothing beside it; no - a 3-word label.

<a id="e2-device"></a>
### device

The brand's signature element on a slide: named by the brand (`layouts[].composition.device`, or a decor element with `frequency: always` on that slide kind) or the L4 `signature` of a reference record.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `device.named` (chain `element`, order 395): not (kind is text); (named) or (signature). Why: the brand names it as its device (or the reference record names it its signature).

Signal: named: true (brand context) or signature: true (L4).

Not to be confused with:
- [decor](#e2-decor): decor holds no text and is not named by the brand; a device is named
- [band](#e2-band): a band is a strip by geometry; a band the brand names is its device

Maps from:
- template: `template.element.role: device`

Examples: yes - a cover band element the brand's cover layout names as its `composition.device`; no - an unnamed corner dot grid.

<a id="e2-background"></a>
### background

A plain fill covering 90 % of the slide or more: the slide's ground.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `background.fill` (chain `element`, order 400): kind is shape; areaPct >= 90. Why: covers >= 90 % of the slide.

Signal: a shape with areaPct >= 90.

Not to be confused with:
- [background-art](#e2-background-art): art is an image / pixel region
- [panel](#e2-panel): a panel is smaller than the slide

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: background`
- template: `template.element.role: background`

Examples: yes - a full-slide purple rectangle; no - a half-slide panel.

<a id="e2-background-art"></a>
### background-art

An image or pixel region covering 90 % of the slide or more.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `background-art.cover` (chain `element`, order 401): kind is image / region; areaPct >= 90. Why: art covering >= 90 % of the slide.

Signal: an image / region with areaPct >= 90.

Not to be confused with:
- [hero-image](#e2-hero-image): a hero image covers 12-90 %
- [background](#e2-background): a plain fill
- [watermark](#e2-watermark): background art is full strength

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.imagery.sample.kind: abstract`
- anatomy: `role: background-art`
- template: `template.element.role: background-art`

Examples: yes - a full-bleed photo behind the title; no - a half-slide photo.

<a id="e2-brand-logo"></a>
### brand-logo

The brand's own mark: a mark whose file is in `brand.logos`; on a reference, a mark repeated as furniture, or a small (< 5 %) wide (aspect >= 1.2) mark in a corner zone with no partner label.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `brand-logo.furniture` (chain `element`, order 410): kind is image / vectorgroup; furniture; areaPct < 5. Why: a small mark repeated on >= 40 % of the deck's pages at this spot.
- `brand-logo.file` (chain `element`, order 425): kind is image / vectorgroup; inLogos = true. Why: its file is one of the brand's logos.
- `brand-logo.corner` (chain `element`, order 430): kind is image / vectorgroup; areaPct < 5; inCorner; aspect >= 1.2. Why: small wide mark in a corner zone.

Signal: inLogos: true; furniture mark; small wide mark in a corner (top / bottom 22 %, left / right 30 %).

Not to be confused with:
- [partner-logo](#e2-partner-logo): a partner logo sits by a partner label, or its file is not a brand logo
- [logo-item](#e2-logo-item): one of 3 or more marks in a grid
- [icon](#e2-icon): a logo is a wide mark in a corner

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: logo`
- brand: `mood.footer.items: logo`, `brand.imagery.sample.kind: logo`, `brand.template.slot.type: logo`
- anatomy: `role: logo`, `role: footer-mark`
- catalogue: `header: .lg`
- template: `template.element.role: brand-logo`, `template.mark.part: lg`

Examples: yes - the wordmark top left of a cover; no - a client logo under "Prepared for".

<a id="e2-partner-logo"></a>
### partner-logo

Another organisation's mark: under or beside a partner label, or (with brand context) a mark whose file is not in `brand.logos`.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `partner-logo.label` (chain `element`, order 420): kind is image / vectorgroup; areaPct < 5; next to a text the rule `label.partner` identified. Why: small mark next to a partner label.
- `partner-logo.not-brand` (chain `element`, order 421): kind is image / vectorgroup; inLogos = false. Why: its file is not one of the brand's logos.

Signal: next to a partner label; inLogos: false.

Not to be confused with:
- [brand-logo](#e2-brand-logo): the brand logo has no partner label and its file is a brand logo

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: logo`
- anatomy: `role: partner-logo`
- template: `template.element.role: partner-logo`

Examples: yes - a client logo right of "Prepared for"; no - the brand wordmark alone in the top-left corner.

<a id="e2-logo-item"></a>
### logo-item

One of 3 or more marks set in a row or grid (a logo wall, client list).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `logo-item.grid` (chain `element`, order 428): kind is image / vectorgroup; areaPct < 5; areaPct >= 0.1; aspect >= 1.2; not holdsText; (kind is image) or (pieces >= 3); peerMarks >= 3. Why: one of >= 3 similar wide marks in a row / grid (an image, or a drawing of 3 pieces or more, holding no text).

Signal: a wide mark (aspect >= 1.2, 0.1 - 5 % of the slide; an image or a drawing of >= 3 pieces; holding no text) with peerMarks >= 3 (such marks of similar height sharing its row or column, itself included).

Not to be confused with:
- [brand-logo](#e2-brand-logo): the brand logo stands alone
- [icon](#e2-icon): icons are square-ish pictograms (aspect under 1.2)
- [decor](#e2-decor): a chart bar is one drawn piece; a mark is an image or a drawing of 3 pieces or more

Maps from:
- content: `content.cell.type: logo`
- template: `template.element.role: logo-item`

Examples: yes - the fourth of eight client logos in a 4 x 2 grid; no - a lone logo in a corner.

<a id="e2-chart-exhibit"></a>
### chart-exhibit

A data exhibit: a chart element, or a vector group of 8 pieces or more over 4 % of the slide holding 3 number labels or more.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `chart-exhibit.vector` (chain `element`, order 440): kind is vectorgroup; pieces >= 8; areaPct >= 4; numberLabelsInside >= 3. Why: many vector pieces holding >= 3 number labels.
- `chart-exhibit.element` (chain `element`, order 445): kind is chart. Why: a chart element.

Signal: deck chart; vectorgroup pieces >= 8, areaPct >= 4, numberLabelsInside >= 3.

Not to be confused with:
- [diagram](#e2-diagram): a diagram holds word labels, not number labels
- [illustration](#e2-illustration): an illustration holds no text
- [table-exhibit](#e2-table-exhibit): a chart draws data as marks

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: chart`
- brand: `brand.template.slot.type: chart`
- anatomy: `role: chart-or-diagram`
- template: `template.element.role: chart-exhibit`

Examples: yes - a bar chart drawn as 24 paths with "12%" labels; no - a process diagram.

<a id="e2-diagram"></a>
### diagram

A drawn structure of boxes, arrows and word labels: a vector group of 8 pieces or more over 4 % holding 2 texts or more (and fewer than 3 number labels).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `diagram.vector` (chain `element`, order 441): kind is vectorgroup; pieces >= 8; areaPct >= 4; textsInside >= 2. Why: many vector pieces holding word labels.

Signal: vectorgroup pieces >= 8, areaPct >= 4, textsInside >= 2.

Not to be confused with:
- [chart-exhibit](#e2-chart-exhibit): a chart holds number labels
- [illustration](#e2-illustration): an illustration holds no text

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: chart-or-diagram`
- template: `template.element.role: diagram`

Examples: yes - a 4-step cycle with node labels; no - a bar chart.

<a id="e2-illustration"></a>
### illustration

Drawn art without text: a vector group of 8 pieces or more over 4 % of the slide holding no text.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `illustration.vector` (chain `element`, order 442): kind is vectorgroup; pieces >= 8; areaPct >= 4. Why: many vector pieces, no labels inside.

Signal: vectorgroup pieces >= 8, areaPct >= 4, no text inside.

Not to be confused with:
- [chart-exhibit](#e2-chart-exhibit): holds number labels
- [diagram](#e2-diagram): holds word labels
- [decor](#e2-decor): decor is a plain fill

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: illustration`, `brand.imagery.sample.kind: illustration`
- anatomy: `role: chart-or-diagram`
- template: `template.element.role: illustration`

Examples: yes - a line drawing of a city skyline; no - a labelled flow chart.

<a id="e2-table-exhibit"></a>
### table-exhibit

A table element: cells in rows and columns.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `table-exhibit.element` (chain `element`, order 446): kind is table. Why: a table element.

Signal: deck table.

Not to be confused with:
- [chart-exhibit](#e2-chart-exhibit): a chart draws data as marks

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: table`
- brand: `brand.template.slot.type: table`
- template: `template.element.role: table-exhibit`

Examples: yes - a 3 x 4 table; no - three cards in a row.

<a id="e2-watermark"></a>
### watermark

A mark or picture set faint (opacity 0.35 or less) over 5 % of the slide or more, behind the content.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `watermark.faint` (chain `element`, order 448): kind is image / vectorgroup; opacity <= 0.35; areaPct >= 5. Why: faint mark over a large area.

Signal: opacity <= 0.35, areaPct >= 5.

Not to be confused with:
- [background-art](#e2-background-art): background art is full strength
- [decor-word](#e2-decor-word): a decor word is text

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: watermark`
- template: `template.element.role: watermark`

Examples: yes - the logo at 8 % opacity across the slide; no - the logo at full strength.

<a id="e2-cutout"></a>
### cutout

An image of 12 % of the slide or more with transparency: a subject cut out of its background.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `cutout.transparent` (chain `element`, order 450): kind is image; areaPct >= 12; transparent. Why: image >= 12 % of the slide with transparency.

Signal: image, areaPct >= 12, transparent.

Not to be confused with:
- [hero-image](#e2-hero-image): a hero image is opaque
- [picture](#e2-picture): a picture is under 12 %

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: cutout`
- template: `template.element.role: cutout`

Examples: yes - a person cut out on the right of a cover; no - a rectangular photo.

<a id="e2-hero-image"></a>
### hero-image

An opaque image covering 12 % of the slide or more (under 90 %).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `hero-image.large` (chain `element`, order 451): kind is image; areaPct >= 12. Why: image >= 12 % of the slide.

Signal: image, 12 <= areaPct < 90, opaque.

Not to be confused with:
- [cutout](#e2-cutout): transparent
- [picture](#e2-picture): under 12 %
- [background-art](#e2-background-art): >= 90 %
- [transparent](#e4-transparent) (E4): a hero image is opaque

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: hero-image`
- template: `template.element.role: hero-image`

Examples: yes - the right-half photo of a cover; no - a team headshot.

<a id="e2-avatar"></a>
### avatar

A small portrait (under 4 % of the slide), square-ish, cut to an ellipse.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `avatar.round` (chain `element`, order 452): kind is image; areaPct < 4; mask = "ellipse". Why: small image cut to a circle.

Signal: image, areaPct < 4, mask ellipse.

Not to be confused with:
- [picture](#e2-picture): a picture is not cut to a circle
- [icon](#e2-icon): an icon is a pictogram

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.components: avatar`
- template: `template.element.role: avatar`

Examples: yes - a 120 px round headshot; no - a square product shot.

<a id="e2-picture"></a>
### picture

An image of 1.5 % to 12 % of the slide.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `picture.size` (chain `element`, order 455): kind is image; areaPct >= 1.5. Why: image, 1.5 % of the slide or more.

Signal: image, 1.5 <= areaPct < 12.

Not to be confused with:
- [hero-image](#e2-hero-image): >= 12 %
- [icon](#e2-icon): < 1.5 %
- [cutout](#e2-cutout): a picture is under 12 %
- [avatar](#e2-avatar): a picture is not cut to a circle

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: image`
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: image`, `brand.imagery.sample.kind: photo-people`, `brand.imagery.sample.kind: photo-product`, `brand.imagery.sample.kind: product-ui`, `brand.template.slot.type: image`
- content: `content.cell.type: image`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: picture`
- template: `template.element.role: picture`

Examples: yes - a card photo; no - a 32 px icon.

<a id="e2-icon"></a>
### icon

A small pictogram: an image or a vector under 1.5 % of the slide.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `icon.image` (chain `element`, order 456): kind is image. Why: image under 1.5 % of the slide.
- `icon.vector` (chain `element`, order 500): kind is vectorgroup; areaPct < 1.5. Why: vector under 1.5 % of the slide.

Signal: image / vectorgroup with areaPct < 1.5.

Not to be confused with:
- [picture](#e2-picture): >= 1.5 %
- [marker](#e2-marker): a marker heads an item
- [brand-logo](#e2-brand-logo): a logo is a wide mark in a corner
- [logo-item](#e2-logo-item): icons are square-ish pictograms (aspect under 1.2)
- [avatar](#e2-avatar): an icon is a pictogram

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: actionIcon`, `brand.cardBlock.type: icon`, `brand.cardBlock.type: rating`, `brand.imagery.sample.kind: icon`, `brand.components: icons`, `brand.components: icon`
- content: `content.cell.type: check`, `content.cell.type: rating`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: icon`
- template: `template.element.role: icon`

Examples: yes - a 40 px line icon over a card heading; no - a card photo.

<a id="e2-sticker"></a>
### sticker

A small element (under 6 %) set at a tilt (3 degrees or more): die-cut art stuck on the slide.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `sticker.tilted` (chain `element`, order 458): not (kind is text); tilt >= 3; areaPct < 6. Why: small and tilted.

Signal: tilt >= 3, areaPct < 6.

Not to be confused with:
- [badge](#e2-badge): a badge is level (no tilt) and holds a short text on the edge of another element

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: sticker`
- template: `template.element.role: sticker`

Examples: yes - a "NEW!" star rotated 12 degrees; no - a level "NEW" pill on a card corner.

<a id="e2-badge"></a>
### badge

A small level shape (under 1.5 %) holding 3 words or fewer, set on the edge of another element.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `badge.on-edge` (chain `element`, order 459): kind is shape / region; holdsText; areaPct < 1.5; heldWords <= 3; onEdge; not (tilt >= 3). Why: small level shape with a short text on the edge of another element.

Signal: shape, holdsText, areaPct < 1.5, heldWords <= 3, onEdge.

Not to be confused with:
- [sticker](#e2-sticker): a sticker is tilted
- [chip](#e2-chip): a chip is a pill in a row / inline, not on an edge

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: badge`, `brand.cardBlock.type: badge`, `brand.components: badge`
- template: `template.element.role: badge`

Examples: yes - a "PRO" tag on the corner of a pricing card; no - a tilted sticker.

<a id="e2-chip"></a>
### chip

A pill (radius >= half its height) under 1.5 % of the slide holding 3 words or fewer: a tag.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `chip.pill` (chain `element`, order 460): kind is shape / region; holdsText; areaPct < 1.5; heldWords <= 3; pill. Why: a small pill holding a short label.

Signal: shape, holdsText, pill, heldWords <= 3.

Not to be confused with:
- [badge](#e2-badge): a badge sits on the edge of another element
- [button](#e2-button): a button says an action
- [card](#e2-card): a pill with a tag

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: tags`, `brand.components: chip`, `brand.components: tags`
- content: `content.cell.type: chip`
- template: `template.element.role: chip`

Examples: yes - a "Fintech" tag pill; no - a "Learn more" button.

<a id="e2-button"></a>
### button

A small shape (under 3 %) holding a call to action of 4 words or fewer ("Learn more", "Get started").

Identified when (in chain order):
- `button.cta` (chain `element`, order 461): kind is shape / region; holdsText; areaPct < 3; heldWords <= 4; heldText matches `cta`. Why: a small shape holding call-to-action wording.

Signal: shape, holdsText, heldText matches `cta`.

Not to be confused with:
- [chip](#e2-chip): a chip labels, a button acts
- [card](#e2-card): a card holds content

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: link`, `brand.cardBlock.type: button`, `brand.components: button`, `brand.components: buttonSecondary`, `brand.components: buttonOutline`, `brand.components: buttonCta`, `brand.components: ctaChevron`
- content: `content.v1.block.type: cta`
- template: `template.element.role: button`

Examples: yes - "Get started" on a filled pill; no - "Fintech" on a pill.

<a id="e2-callout"></a>
### callout

A fill holding text with a pointer (a tail or arrow) aimed at another element.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `callout.pointer` (chain `element`, order 462): kind is shape / region; holdsText; pointer. Why: a text fill with a pointer.

Signal: shape, holdsText, pointer.

Not to be confused with:
- [card](#e2-card): a card has no pointer
- [panel](#e2-panel): a panel has no pointer

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.components: callout`
- template: `template.element.role: callout`

Examples: yes - a speech-bubble note pointing at a chart peak; no - a card.

<a id="e2-pager"></a>
### pager

A row of 3 or more equal small marks or numbers in the top / bottom band showing where the slide sits in the deck (dots, bars, a track).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `pager.series` (chain `element`, order 463): series >= 3; (y0 > 85) or (y1 < 15). Why: one of >= 3 equal small marks in a row at the top / bottom.

Signal: series >= 3 in the top / bottom 15 % band.

Not to be confused with:
- [page-number](#e2-page-number): a page number is one number
- [tabs](#e2-tabs): tabs are words

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.components: pager`, `brand.components: progress`
- template: `template.element.role: pager`

Examples: yes - five dots bottom centre, the third filled; no - one page number.

<a id="e2-tabs"></a>
### tabs

A row of 2 or more short texts (3 words or fewer) near the top, one of them marked active.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `tabs.row` (chain `element`, order 199): kind is text; rowPeers >= 2; activePeer; words <= 3. Why: one of a row of short texts with one marked active.

Signal: rowPeers >= 2, activePeer.

Not to be confused with:
- [pager](#e2-pager): a pager is marks
- [label](#e2-label): labels name things, nothing is active

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.components: linkBar`, `brand.components: tabs`
- template: `template.element.role: tabs`

Examples: yes - "Overview | Pricing | FAQ" with Pricing underlined; no - three column headings.

<a id="e2-marker"></a>
### marker

A small number, dot or icon shape at the head of an item (01, a bullet square, a step circle).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `marker.text` (chain `element`, order 75): kind is text; itemHead; words <= 2. Why: a short text at the head of an item.
- `marker.shape` (chain `element`, order 466): not (kind is text); itemHead; areaPct < 1. Why: a small shape at the head of an item.

Signal: itemHead, small (areaPct < 1) or a short text.

Not to be confused with:
- [icon](#e2-icon): an icon is not tied to an item head
- [connector](#e2-connector): a connector joins markers

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.steps.marker: circle-number`, `brand.steps.marker: square-number`, `brand.steps.marker: dot`, `brand.steps.marker: icon`, `brand.steps.marker: chevron`
- template: `template.element.role: marker`

Examples: yes - "01" over a card heading; no - a lone dot in the background.

<a id="e2-connector"></a>
### connector

A thin shape joining 2 or more markers or items of one block (a timeline axis, a step line).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `connector.joins` (chain `element`, order 467): not (kind is text); thin; length >= 2.5; joinsItems >= 2. Why: a thin line joining >= 2 items of one block.

Signal: thin, joinsItems >= 2.

Not to be confused with:
- [divider](#e2-divider): a divider separates groups, a connector joins items
- [rule](#e2-rule): a rule touches no item
- [marker](#e2-marker): a connector joins markers

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.components: arrow`
- template: `template.element.role: connector`

Examples: yes - the line through four timeline dots; no - a hairline between two columns.

<a id="e2-divider"></a>
### divider

A thin shape (< 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick, 2.5 % long or more) with content on both sides along its length, at least half as long as the wider side: it separates two groups.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `divider.between` (chain `element`, order 470): not (kind is text); thin; length >= 2.5; sidesWithContent = 2. Why: thin line with content on both sides along its length.

Signal: thin, length >= 2.5, sidesWithContent = 2.

Not to be confused with:
- [rule](#e2-rule): a rule has content on one side or none (an accent under a title)
- [connector](#e2-connector): a connector joins items

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: divider`
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: divider`, `brand.gradient.use: divider`, `brand.components: divider`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: rule`
- template: `template.element.role: divider`

Examples: yes - a vertical hairline between two text columns; no - a short accent bar under a title.

<a id="e2-rule"></a>
### rule

A thin shape (< 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick, 2.5 % long or more) that separates nothing: an accent line, a hairline above a footer.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `rule.thin` (chain `element`, order 471): not (kind is text); thin; length >= 2.5. Why: thin line, 2.5 % of the slide long or more.

Signal: thin, length >= 2.5, sidesWithContent < 2.

Not to be confused with:
- [divider](#e2-divider): a divider has content on both sides
- [band](#e2-band): a band is thick
- [connector](#e2-connector): a rule touches no item

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: rule`, `brand.layout.divider: rule`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: rule`
- catalogue: `header: .r`
- template: `template.element.role: rule`, `template.mark.part: r`

Examples: yes - a 150 px accent rule under a title; no - a column divider.

<a id="e2-frame"></a>
### frame

An outline (stroke, no fill) drawn around an image or a group of content.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `frame.outline` (chain `element`, order 465): kind is shape / region; stroke; not fill; framesContent. Why: an outline around content.

Signal: shape, stroke, no fill, framesContent.

Not to be confused with:
- [card](#e2-card): a card is filled
- [decor](#e2-decor): decor encloses nothing
- [device-frame](#e4-device-frame) (E4): an E2 frame is an outline; a device frame is a drawn device

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: frame`, `brand.gradient.use: border`
- template: `template.element.role: frame`

Examples: yes - a 2 px border around a photo; no - a filled card.

<a id="e2-cut-shape"></a>
### cut-shape

A filled shape with a non-axis edge (a slant; its angle is recorded).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `cut-shape.angle` (chain `element`, order 480): kind is shape / region; angles. Why: filled shape with a non-axis edge.

Signal: shape with angles.

Not to be confused with:
- [band](#e2-band): a band is axis-aligned
- [panel](#e2-panel): a panel is axis-aligned

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: cut-shape`
- template: `template.element.role: cut-shape`

Examples: yes - a white wedge cut at 10 degrees across a cover; no - a rectangle.

<a id="e2-band"></a>
### band

A strip spanning a full side (full width up to 30 % H, or full height up to 40 % W) holding no text or only furniture.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `band.strip` (chain `element`, order 490): kind is shape / region; spansSide; heldTexts <= 0. Why: full-width / full-height strip holding no text (furniture aside).

Signal: spansSide, heldTexts = 0.

Not to be confused with:
- [panel](#e2-panel): a panel holds text
- [decor](#e2-decor): decor does not span a side
- [device](#e2-device): a band is a strip by geometry; a band the brand names is its device
- [rule](#e2-rule): a band is thick
- [cut-shape](#e2-cut-shape): a band is axis-aligned

Maps from:
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: band`
- template: `template.element.role: band`

Examples: yes - a 12 % H full-width colour strip at the bottom; no - a full-width strip holding the title (a panel).

<a id="e2-panel"></a>
### panel

A fill holding text, 8 % of the slide or more.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `panel.large` (chain `element`, order 495): kind is shape / region; holdsText; areaPct >= 8. Why: large fill holding text.

Signal: shape, holdsText, areaPct >= 8.

Not to be confused with:
- [card](#e2-card): under 8 %
- [band](#e2-band): a band holds no text
- [callout](#e2-callout): a callout has a pointer
- [background](#e2-background): a panel is smaller than the slide
- [cut-shape](#e2-cut-shape): a panel is axis-aligned

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardBlock.type: panel`, `brand.layout.divider: panel`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: panel`
- template: `template.element.role: panel`, `template.emphasis.carrier: colour-field`

Examples: yes - a purple block holding the cover title; no - a small card.

<a id="e2-card"></a>
### card

A fill holding text, under 8 % of the slide.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `card.small` (chain `element`, order 496): kind is shape / region; holdsText. Why: fill holding text.

Signal: shape, holdsText, areaPct < 8.

Not to be confused with:
- [panel](#e2-panel): >= 8 %
- [chip](#e2-chip): a pill with a tag
- [button](#e2-button): an action
- [callout](#e2-callout): a card has no pointer
- [frame](#e2-frame): a card is filled

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.components: cards`, `brand.components: card`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: card`
- template: `template.element.role: card`

Examples: yes - one of three feature cards; no - a half-slide panel.

<a id="e2-decor"></a>
### decor

Everything drawn that holds no text and that no other rule names (a fill, a vector shape).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `decor.fill` (chain `element`, order 499): kind is shape / region / line. Why: fill holding no text.
- `decor.vector` (chain `element`, order 501): kind is vectorgroup. Why: vector over 1.5 % of the slide, no other rule.

Signal: a shape / region / line / vector no earlier rule took.

Not to be confused with:
- [device](#e2-device): a device is named by the brand
- [band](#e2-band): a band spans a side
- [quote-mark](#e2-quote-mark): a drawn quote shape is decor unless named
- [logo-item](#e2-logo-item): a chart bar is one drawn piece; a mark is an image or a drawing of 3 pieces or more
- [illustration](#e2-illustration): decor is a plain fill
- [frame](#e2-frame): decor encloses nothing

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: decor`
- brand: `brand.decor.type: shape`, `brand.gradient.use: glow`
- anatomy: `role: footer-mark`, `role: decor`
- template: `template.element.role: decor`

Examples: yes - a circle bottom right; no - a full-width strip.

## E3 - structure: what things form together

<a id="e3-cell"></a>
### cell (composition)

One box of a table or grid: the crossing of a row and a column. A table row (catalogue field `row`) is identified as its cells.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `cell.row` (chain `element`, order 50): inBlock; cells >= 2. Why: a field of a block holding two or more cells: a table row.
- `cell.grid` (chain `structure`, order 70): row; col. Why: a member with both a row and a column index.

Signal: a field holding two or more cells (td / th); a member of a grid with a row and a column index.

Not to be confused with:
- [item](#e3-item): an item is one repeated unit of a list block; a cell sits in a row AND a column

Maps from:
- catalogue: `data-f: row`
- template: `template.element.structure: cell`

Examples: yes - a table row "Fintechs | $504B | 22%"; no - a bullet line.

<a id="e3-table-block"></a>
### table-block (block)

Rows of cells under a header row (content/2 `table`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `table-block.cells` (chain `block`, order 10): termCount.cell > 0. Why: its fields are rows of cells.

Signal: a field identified as cell.

Not to be confused with:
- [compare](#e3-compare): a compare is two items of heading + description

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.slot.type: table`
- brand: `brand.template.region.kind: table`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: table`, `content.v1.block.type: table`
- catalogue: `data-type: table`
- template: `template.element.structure: table-block`

Examples: yes - a 4-column table of figures; no - three KPI tiles.

<a id="e3-kpis"></a>
### kpis (block)

Figures with their explanation (content/2 `kpis`): items holding a big-number, with a body, and a heading or not.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `kpis.figures` (chain `block`, order 20): itemShare.big-number >= 0.5. Why: half of its items or more hold a big-number.

Signal: itemShare.big-number >= 0.5.

Not to be confused with:
- [items](#e3-items): items lead with a heading, not a figure
- [chart-block](#e3-chart-block): a chart draws its figures

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: kpis`, `layout.slot.type: kpis`
- brand: `brand.cardRecipe.kind: stat`, `brand.template.region.kind: kpi`, `brand.components: kpi`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: kpis`, `content.v1.block.type: kpis`
- catalogue: `data-type: kpi_block`, `data-type: kpi_vb`
- template: `template.element.structure: kpis`

Examples: yes - three tiles "$504B / Global revenue / ..."; no - three cards with headings.

<a id="e3-chart-block"></a>
### chart-block (block)

A data exhibit drawn over its labels (content/2 `chart`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `chart-block.labels` (chain `block`, order 30): termShare.label = 1. Why: every field is a short label over a drawn area.

Signal: termShare.label = 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [points](#e3-points): a list shows no data labels of its own
- [kpis](#e3-kpis): KPIs set their figures as marked fields

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.chart.chartType: bar`, `deck.chart.chartType: column`, `deck.chart.chartType: stackedBar`, `deck.chart.chartType: line`, `deck.chart.chartType: area`, `deck.chart.chartType: pie`, `deck.chart.chartType: donut`, `deck.chart.chartType: scatter`, `deck.chart.form: funnel`, `deck.chart.form: waterfall`, `deck.chart.form: radar`, `deck.chart.form: gauge`
- layout: `layout.slot.type: chart`
- brand: `brand.template.region.kind: chart`, `brand.gradient.use: chartSeries`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: chart`, `content.v1.block.type: chart`, `content.chart.chartType: column`, `content.chart.chartType: bar`, `content.chart.chartType: line`, `content.chart.chartType: area`, `content.chart.chartType: pie`, `content.chart.chartType: donut`, `content.chart.chartType: stacked`, `content.chart.chartType: grouped`, `content.chart.chartType: stacked%`, `content.chart.chartType: funnel`, `content.chart.chartType: waterfall`, `content.chart.chartType: scatter`, `content.chart.chartType: radar`, `content.chart.chartType: gauge`, `content.chart.chartType: stackedBar`
- catalogue: `data-type: chart`
- template: `template.element.structure: chart-block`

Examples: yes - a column chart with "2024 / 2025" labels; no - a bullet list.

<a id="e3-paragraph-block"></a>
### paragraph-block (block)

One run of running text (content/2 `paragraph`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `paragraph-block.text` (chain `block`, order 40): termShare.paragraph = 1. Why: its one field is a paragraph.

Signal: termShare.paragraph = 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [points](#e3-points): points are several items
- [quotes](#e3-quotes): a paragraph is not quoted

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.slot.type: richtext`
- brand: `brand.template.region.kind: paragraph`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: paragraph`, `content.v1.block.type: paragraph`
- catalogue: `data-type: paragraph`
- template: `template.element.structure: paragraph-block`

Examples: yes - a 3-line takeaway; no - a 4-line list.

<a id="e3-points"></a>
### points (block)

A list of single lines (content/2 `points`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `points.bullets` (chain `block`, order 50): termShare.bullet = 1. Why: every field is a bullet.

Signal: termShare.bullet = 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [items](#e3-items): items have a heading + description each
- [chart-block](#e3-chart-block): chart labels belong to a block showing data labels
- [paragraph-block](#e3-paragraph-block): points are several items

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.box.role: list`, `layout.slot.type: list`
- brand: `brand.cardRecipe.kind: list`, `brand.template.region.kind: list`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: points`, `content.v1.block.type: list`
- catalogue: `data-type: simple_list`
- template: `template.element.structure: points`

Examples: yes - four ticked action lines; no - three cards.

<a id="e3-timeline"></a>
### timeline (block)

Items in time order, each labelled by a date or period (content/2 `timeline`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `timeline.periods` (chain `block`, order 60): minItemFields >= 2; (labelText matches `period`) or (headText matches `periodStart`). Why: its items are labelled by dates / periods (2024, Q1 2026, Feb 2025, Now).

Signal: labelText matches `period`, or the first heading starts with one.

Not to be confused with:
- [process](#e3-process): process steps are ordinals (Step 1), not dates
- [items](#e3-items): items carry no period
- [subpoints](#e3-subpoints): a timeline with lists is labelled by periods first

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.slot.type: timeline`
- brand: `brand.components: timeline`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: timeline`, `content.v1.block.type: timeline`
- catalogue: `data-type: roadmap`, `data-type: timeline`, `data-type: timeline_with_list`
- template: `template.element.structure: timeline`

Examples: yes - "2024 Listings stall | 2025 Listings return"; no - "Step 1 Payments first | Step 2 ...".

<a id="e3-process"></a>
### process (block)

Steps in order: each labelled by an ordinal (Step 1, Phase 2, Stage 3), or joined in sequence by a connector line (content/2 `process`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `process.ordinals` (chain `block`, order 65): minItemFields >= 2; labelText matches `ordinal`. Why: its items are labelled by step ordinals.
- `process.connector` (chain `block`, order 85): minItemFields >= 2; (items >= 2 and connector.crossing >= items) or (connector.inner > 0); labelText. Why: a connector line joins every item (one line crosses each of them) or runs through them in pieces, and the first item carries a label: a sequence. Period labels were already decided as timeline (timeline.periods), ordinals as process (process.ordinals); a sequence with any other label (01, a region) is a process. A frame rule over an unlabelled row (a comparison, a column list) is not a connector: the label is required (V1, the answer key: without it 3 lists and 3 column lists turn process).

Signal: labelText matches `ordinal`; or connector.crossing = items (or connector.inner > 0) with a label on the first item.

Not to be confused with:
- [timeline](#e3-timeline): a timeline is labelled by dates
- [items](#e3-items): items may be numbered 01 / 02 without being steps; a connector line joining every labelled item makes them a sequence (a numbered row under one rule drawn as a list is not separable by any visible sign: L1-35)

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.slot.type: steps`
- brand: `brand.components: steps`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: process`, `content.v1.block.type: steps`, `content.process.shape: linear`, `content.process.shape: cycle`, `content.process.shape: funnel`, `content.process.shape: pyramid`, `content.process.shape: stack`, `content.process.shape: hub`, `content.process.shape: ladder`, `content.process.shape: quadrant`, `content.process.shape: venn`, `content.process.shape: tree`, `content.process.shape: converge`, `content.process.shape: diverge`
- catalogue: `data-type: roadmap`
- template: `template.element.structure: process`

Examples: yes - "Step 1 Structured data | Step 2 Earned trust"; no - "2024 | 2025".

<a id="e3-subpoints"></a>
### subpoints (block)

Items whose explanation is a list of sub-points (content/2 `subpoints`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `subpoints.lists` (chain `block`, order 70): minItemFields >= 2; listItemShare >= 0.5. Why: half of its items or more explain their heading with two runs or more.

Signal: listItemShare >= 0.5.

Not to be confused with:
- [items](#e3-items): an item explains with one run of text
- [timeline](#e3-timeline): a timeline with lists is labelled by periods first

Maps from:
- content: `content.v2.block.type: subpoints`
- catalogue: `data-type: list_with_subpoints`
- template: `template.element.structure: subpoints`

Examples: yes - "Proven in workflows" with two ruled sub-lines; no - a heading with one description.

<a id="e3-compare"></a>
### compare (block)

Two sides set against each other (content/2 `compare`): two items side by side with a rule between them, or labelled as a contrast (From / Then / Before).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `compare.contrast` (chain `block`, order 59): minItemFields >= 2; items = 2; labelText matches `contrast`. Why: two items, the first labelled as one side of a contrast (From, Then, Before ...).
- `compare.two-sides` (chain `block`, order 80): minItemFields >= 2; items = 2; itemsInRow; between; not numbered. Why: exactly two items side by side with a rule between them, not numbered.

Signal: items = 2 side by side with a rule between; a contrast label.

Not to be confused with:
- [items](#e3-items): items are a set: stacked, or without a rule between, or numbered
- [table-block](#e3-table-block): a compare is two items of heading + description

Maps from:
- content: `content.v2.block.type: compare`
- catalogue: `data-type: comparison`
- template: `template.element.structure: compare`

Examples: yes - "Digitally enhanced | AI-first operations" either side of a hairline; no - two numbered cards.

Items each with a heading and a description (content/2 `items`, the catalogue list with description and multi-column list).

Signal: minItemFields >= 2.

Not to be confused with:

- brand: `brand.cardRecipe.kind: feature`, `brand.cardRecipe.kind: case_study`, `brand.cardRecipe.kind: pricing`, `brand.cardRecipe.kind: blog`, `brand.cardRecipe.kind: listing`, `brand.template.slot.type: cards`, `brand.template.region.kind: cards`
- content: `content.v2.block.type: items`, `content.v1.block.type: cards`
- catalogue: `data-type: list_with_description`, `data-type: multi_column_list`
- template: `template.element.structure: items`

Examples: yes - three cards "Answers, not links / ..."; no - a bullet list.
