<a id="e3-comparison-slide"></a>
### comparison-slide (kind)

Two sides set against each other (a compare block).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `comparison.block` (chain `kind`, order 147): blocks.compare >= 1. Why: holds a compare block.

Signal: blocks.compare >= 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [two-column-slide](#e3-two-column-slide): parallel columns, not opposed

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.kind: comparison`
- template: `template.category: comparison-slide`

Examples: yes - before / after columns; no - two text columns.

<a id="e3-diagram-slide"></a>
### diagram-slide (kind)

A slide built on a diagram (a process / cycle / tree drawing with word labels).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `diagram.drawing` (chain `kind`, order 148): diagrams >= 1. Why: holds a diagram.

Signal: diagrams >= 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [chart-slide](#e3-chart-slide): number labels

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.kind: diagram`
- template: `template.category: diagram-slide`

Examples: yes - a 4-step cycle; no - a bar chart.

<a id="e3-timeline-slide"></a>
### timeline-slide (kind)

A slide built on a timeline block.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `timeline.block` (chain `kind`, order 149): blocks.timeline >= 1. Why: holds a timeline block.

Signal: blocks.timeline >= 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [steps-slide](#e3-steps-slide): ordinals

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.kind: timeline`
- template: `template.category: timeline-slide`

Examples: yes - 2024 / 2025 / 2026 milestones; no - Step 1 / 2 / 3.

<a id="e3-steps-slide"></a>
### steps-slide (kind)

A slide built on a process block (ordinal steps).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `steps.block` (chain `kind`, order 151): blocks.process >= 1. Why: holds a process block.

Signal: blocks.process >= 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [timeline-slide](#e3-timeline-slide): dates

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.kind: steps`
- template: `template.category: steps-slide`

Examples: yes - Step 1 / 2 / 3; no - 2024 / 2025.

<a id="e3-logos-slide"></a>
### logos-slide (kind)

A logo wall: 3 logo items or more.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `logos.wall` (chain `kind`, order 152): logoItems >= 3. Why: >= 3 logo items.

Signal: logoItems >= 3.

Not to be confused with:
- [team-slide](#e3-team-slide): portraits

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.kind: logos`
- template: `template.category: logos-slide`

Examples: yes - eight client logos; no - four headshots.

<a id="e3-image-slide"></a>
### image-slide (kind)

A picture slide: a full or near-full image with 10 words or fewer.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `image.full` (chain `kind`, order 155): photos >= 1; words <= 10. Why: a photo with <= 10 words.

Signal: photos >= 1, words <= 10.

Not to be confused with:
- [image-text-slide](#e3-image-text-slide): a photo with text

Maps from:
- layout: `layout.kind: image`
- template: `template.category: image-slide`

Examples: yes - a full-bleed photo with a caption; no - a photo beside bullets.

## E4 - treatment: how a thing is finished

<a id="e4-device-frame"></a>
### device-frame (image-treatment)

An image set inside a device mockup (a phone / laptop / browser frame) (content/2 treatment `device`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `device-frame.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 1): inDevice. Why: sits inside a device frame.

Signal: inDevice.

Not to be confused with:
- [frame](#e2-frame) (E2): an E2 frame is an outline; a device frame is a drawn device

Maps from:
- content: `content.image.treatment: device`
- template: `template.element.treatment: device-frame`

Examples: yes - a UI screenshot in a phone; no - a photo with a border.

<a id="e4-transparent"></a>
### transparent (image-treatment)

A subject cut out of its background (transparent pixels).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `transparent.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 2): transparent. Why: transparent.

Signal: transparent.

Not to be confused with:
- [clipped](#e4-clipped): a clip cuts by a shape, a cut-out by the subject
- [hero-image](#e2-hero-image) (E2): a hero image is opaque

Maps from:
- template: `template.element.treatment: transparent`

Examples: yes - a person on a transparent PNG; no - a rectangular photo.

<a id="e4-clipped"></a>
### clipped (image-treatment)

An image cut to a non-rectangular outline (ellipse, polygon, svg, text).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `clipped.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 3): mask; not (mask = "rect"). Why: masked by a non-rectangular shape.

Signal: mask != rect.

Not to be confused with:
- [transparent](#e4-transparent): transparent pixels
- [side](#e4-side): a plain rectangle

Maps from:
- template: `template.element.treatment: clipped`

Examples: yes - a photo in a circle; no - a rectangular photo.

<a id="e4-collage"></a>
### collage (image-treatment)

Two images or more set together in one block.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `collage.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 4): groupImages >= 2. Why: one of >= 2 images in its block.

Signal: groupImages >= 2.

Not to be confused with:
- [side](#e4-side): one image

Maps from:
- content: `content.image.treatment: collage`
- template: `template.element.treatment: collage`

Examples: yes - three photos in a mosaic; no - one photo.

<a id="e4-background-image"></a>
### background-image (image-treatment)

An image covering 90 % of the slide or more with text over it (content/2 treatment `background`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `background-image.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 5): areaPct >= 90; textOver. Why: covers the slide, text over it.

Signal: areaPct >= 90, textOver.

Not to be confused with:
- [full](#e4-full): a full image has no text over it

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.gradient.use: background`
- content: `content.image.treatment: background`
- template: `template.element.treatment: background-image`

Examples: yes - a tinted photo behind the title; no - a full-bleed photo alone.

<a id="e4-full"></a>
### full (image-treatment)

An image covering 90 % of the slide or more with no text over it (content/2 treatment `full`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `full.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 6): areaPct >= 90. Why: covers the slide.

Signal: areaPct >= 90.

Not to be confused with:
- [background-image](#e4-background-image): text over it
- [side](#e4-side): covers the slide

Maps from:
- content: `content.image.treatment: full`
- template: `template.element.treatment: full`

Examples: yes - a full-bleed photo slide; no - a half-slide photo.

<a id="e4-side"></a>
### side (image-treatment)

An image of 12 % of the slide or more beside the text, run to at least one slide edge (content/2 treatment `side`).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `side.image-treatment` (chain `image-treatment`, order 7): areaPct >= 12; bleedCount >= 1. Why: large, beside the text, bleeds one side or more.

Signal: areaPct >= 12, bleedCount >= 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [full](#e4-full): covers the slide
- [clipped](#e4-clipped): a plain rectangle
- [collage](#e4-collage): one image

Maps from:
- content: `content.image.treatment: side`
- template: `template.element.treatment: side`

Examples: yes - the right half of a slide; no - a card photo.

<a id="e4-rect"></a>
### rect (mask)

A rectangular outline (radius under half the short side).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `rect.mask` (chain `mask`, order 127): outline = "rect". Why: rectangular outline.

Signal: outline = rect.

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.shape.kind: rect`
- layout: `layout.box.shape.kind: rect`
- brand: `brand.mask.type: rect`
- template: `template.element.treatment: rect`

Examples: yes - an image clipped to a rect; no - an unclipped image.

<a id="e4-ellipse"></a>
### ellipse (mask)

An elliptical outline (a circle when square).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `ellipse.mask` (chain `mask`, order 128): outline = "ellipse". Why: elliptical outline.

Signal: outline = ellipse.

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.shape.kind: ellipse`
- layout: `layout.box.shape.kind: ellipse`
- brand: `brand.mask.type: ellipse`
- template: `template.element.treatment: ellipse`

Examples: yes - an image clipped to a ellipse; no - an unclipped image.

<a id="e4-polygon"></a>
### polygon (mask)

A straight-edged outline with a non-axis edge (a slant).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `polygon.mask` (chain `mask`, order 129): outline = "polygon". Why: straight edges at an angle.

Signal: outline = polygon.

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.shape.kind: polygon`
- brand: `brand.mask.type: polygon`
- template: `template.element.treatment: polygon`

Examples: yes - an image clipped to a polygon; no - an unclipped image.

<a id="e4-svg"></a>
### svg (mask)

A free path outline from a vector file.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `svg.mask` (chain `mask`, order 130): outline = "svg". Why: a free path.

Signal: outline = svg.

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.shape.kind: path`
- brand: `brand.mask.type: svg`
- template: `template.element.treatment: svg`

Examples: yes - an image clipped to a svg; no - an unclipped image.

<a id="e4-text-mask"></a>
### text-mask (mask)

The glyphs of a text used as the clip.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `text-mask.mask` (chain `mask`, order 131): outline = "text". Why: clipped to glyphs.

Signal: outline = text.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.mask.type: text`
- template: `template.element.treatment: text-mask`

Examples: yes - an image clipped to a text; no - an unclipped image.

<a id="e4-glass"></a>
### glass (card-style)

A translucent fill over a blur (frosted).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `glass.card-style` (chain `card-style`, order 1): blur; fillAlpha < 1. Why: translucent over a blur.

Signal: blur, fillAlpha < 1.

Not to be confused with:
- [filled](#e4-filled): opaque

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardStyle.kind: glass`
- template: `template.element.treatment: glass`

Examples: yes - a frosted card on a photo; no - a solid card.

<a id="e4-accent"></a>
### accent (card-style)

A card marked by a coloured bar on one side.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `accent.card-style` (chain `card-style`, order 2): accentBar. Why: a bar on one side.

Signal: accentBar.

Not to be confused with:
- [outlined](#e4-outlined): a border on all sides

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardStyle.kind: accent`
- template: `template.element.treatment: accent`

Examples: yes - a card with a 6 px left bar; no - a bordered card.

<a id="e4-elevated"></a>
### elevated (card-style)

A card lifted by a shadow.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `elevated.card-style` (chain `card-style`, order 3): shadow. Why: casts a shadow.

Signal: shadow.

Not to be confused with:
- [flat](#e4-flat): no shadow

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardStyle.kind: elevated`
- template: `template.element.treatment: elevated`

Examples: yes - a white card with a soft shadow; no - a flat card.

<a id="e4-outlined"></a>
### outlined (card-style)

A card drawn by its border, its fill the same as the ground.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `outlined.card-style` (chain `card-style`, order 4): border; not fillDiffers. Why: a border, no fill of its own.

Signal: border, not fillDiffers.

Not to be confused with:
- [filled](#e4-filled): a fill of its own
- [accent](#e4-accent): a border on all sides

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardStyle.kind: outlined`
- template: `template.element.treatment: outlined`

Examples: yes - a hairline-bordered card; no - a grey card.

<a id="e4-filled"></a>
### filled (card-style)

A card with a fill of its own (different from the ground).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `filled.card-style` (chain `card-style`, order 5): fillDiffers. Why: a fill of its own.

Signal: fillDiffers.

Not to be confused with:
- [flat](#e4-flat): same as the ground
- [glass](#e4-glass): opaque
- [outlined](#e4-outlined): a fill of its own

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardStyle.kind: filled`
- template: `template.element.treatment: filled`

Examples: yes - a grey card on white; no - a white card on white.

<a id="e4-flat"></a>
### flat (card-style)

A card with no fill, border or shadow of its own: text grouped by space alone.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `flat.card-style` (chain `card-style`, order 6): not fillDiffers; not border; not shadow. Why: nothing marks it but space.

Signal: no fill / border / shadow.

Not to be confused with:
- [filled](#e4-filled): a fill
- [elevated](#e4-elevated): no shadow

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.cardStyle.kind: flat`
- template: `template.element.treatment: flat`

Examples: yes - a text group on the ground; no - a grey card.

### none (fill)

No paint (transparent).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `none.fill` (chain `fill`, order 1): paint = "none". Why: painted as none.

Signal: paint = none.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.fill.type: none`
- template: `template.element.treatment: none`

Examples: yes - a none fill; no - another paint.

### solid (fill)

- `solid.fill` (chain `fill`, order 2): paint = "solid". Why: painted as solid.

Maps from:

- template: `template.element.treatment: solid`

### linear-gradient (fill)

A gradient along a line.

- `linear-gradient.fill` (chain `fill`, order 3): paint = "linear". Why: painted as linear.

Signal: paint = linear.

Maps from:

- brand: `brand.gradient.type: linear`, `brand.background.type: linear-gradient`, `brand.fill.type: linear-gradient`

<a id="e4-radial-gradient"></a>
### radial-gradient (fill)

A gradient out from a point.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `radial-gradient.fill` (chain `fill`, order 4): paint = "radial". Why: painted as radial.

Signal: paint = radial.

Maps from:

- brand: `brand.gradient.type: radial`, `brand.background.type: radial-gradient`, `brand.fill.type: radial-gradient`

<a id="e4-conic-gradient"></a>
### conic-gradient (fill)

A gradient around a point.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `conic-gradient.fill` (chain `fill`, order 5): paint = "conic". Why: painted as conic.

Signal: paint = conic.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.gradient.type: conic`
- template: `template.element.treatment: conic-gradient`

<a id="e4-mesh-gradient"></a>
### mesh-gradient (fill)

A gradient over a mesh of points.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `mesh-gradient.fill` (chain `fill`, order 6): paint = "mesh". Why: painted as mesh.

Signal: paint = mesh.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.gradient.type: mesh`, `brand.background.type: mesh-gradient`
- template: `template.element.treatment: mesh-gradient`

Examples: yes - a mesh-gradient fill; no - another paint.

<a id="e4-gradient"></a>
### gradient (fill)

Colour stops whose geometry is not given (a gradient of unstated kind).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `gradient.fill` (chain `fill`, order 7): paint = "gradient". Why: painted as gradient.

Signal: paint = gradient.

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.background.type: gradient`

### pattern (fill)

A repeated tile.

- `pattern.fill` (chain `fill`, order 8): paint = "pattern". Why: painted as pattern.

Maps from:

- template: `template.element.treatment: pattern`

<a id="e4-texture"></a>
### texture (fill)

A photographic surface (grain, paper, noise).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `texture.fill` (chain `fill`, order 9): paint = "texture". Why: painted as texture.

Signal: paint = texture.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.decor.type: texture`
- template: `template.element.treatment: texture`

<a id="e4-image-fill"></a>
### image-fill (fill)

- `image-fill.fill` (chain `fill`, order 10): paint = "image". Why: painted as image.

Maps from:

<a id="e4-video"></a>
### video (fill)

A moving picture used as the paint.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `video.fill` (chain `fill`, order 11): paint = "video". Why: painted as video.

Signal: paint = video.

Maps from:

<a id="e4-face-run"></a>
### face-run (emphasis)

A run set in another face than its text.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `face-run.emphasis` (chain `emphasis`, order 1): faceDiffers. Why: another face.

Signal: faceDiffers.

Not to be confused with:

Maps from:

<a id="e4-weight-run"></a>
### weight-run (emphasis)

A run set heavier (or lighter) than its text, same face.

Identified when (in chain order):

Not to be confused with:

- template: `template.element.treatment: weight-run`, `template.emphasis.carrier: weight-run`

<a id="e4-colour-run"></a>
### colour-run (emphasis)

A run set in another colour than its text.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `colour-run.emphasis` (chain `emphasis`, order 3): colourDiffers. Why: another colour.

Not to be confused with:

<a id="e4-angle"></a>
### angle (angle)

A shape cut on a slant: a non-axis edge (its angle recorded, 0-90 degrees from horizontal).

Identified when (in chain order):

Signal: angles.

Maps from:
- template: `template.element.treatment: angle`

Examples: yes - a wedge at 10 degrees; no - a rectangle.

<a id="e4-behind"></a>
### behind (layer)

Drawn under the text it overlaps.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `behind.layer` (chain `layer`, order 1): behindText. Why: under the text it overlaps.

Signal: behindText.

Not to be confused with:
- [front](#e4-front): over the text

Maps from:
- brand: `mood.decor.layer: behind`, `brand.decor.layer: behind`, `brand.cardBlock.layer: back`
- template: `template.element.treatment: behind`, `template.device.layer: behind`

Examples: yes - a decor circle under the title; no - a sticker over the title.

<a id="e4-front"></a>
### front (layer)

Drawn over the text it overlaps.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `front.layer` (chain `layer`, order 2): overText. Why: over the text it overlaps.

Signal: overText.

Not to be confused with:
- [behind](#e4-behind): under the text

Maps from:
- brand: `mood.decor.layer: front`, `brand.decor.layer: front`, `brand.cardBlock.layer: front`
- template: `template.element.treatment: front`, `template.device.layer: front`

Examples: yes - a sticker over the title; no - a background photo.

<a id="e4-bleed"></a>
### bleed (bleed)

Runs off one slide edge or more.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `bleed.bleed` (chain `bleed`, order 1): bleedCount >= 1. Why: touches / crosses a slide edge.

Signal: bleedCount >= 1.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.placement: full-bleed`
- template: `template.element.treatment: bleed`

Examples: yes - a photo to the right edge; no - an inset photo.

<a id="e4-blend"></a>
### blend (blend)

Mixed with what is under it by a blend mode other than normal (multiply, screen, overlay, soft-light ...).

Identified when (in chain order):
- `blend.blend` (chain `blend`, order 1): blend; not (blend = "normal"). Why: a blend mode other than normal.

Signal: blend != normal.

Maps from:
- brand: `brand.blend: normal`, `brand.blend: multiply`, `brand.blend: screen`, `brand.blend: overlay`, `brand.blend: soft-light`, `brand.blend: plus-lighter`, `brand.gradient.use: overlay`
- template: `template.element.treatment: blend`

Examples: yes - a multiply tint over a photo; no - a normal overlay.

<a id="e4-case"></a>
### case (case)

Text set in a case transform (upper, lower, title, sentence) rather than as typed.

Identified when (in chain order):
- `case.case` (chain `case`, order 1): (caps) or (caseTransform). Why: a case transform.

Signal: caps / caseTransform.

Maps from:
- deck: `deck.text.case: none`, `deck.text.case: upper`, `deck.text.case: lower`, `deck.text.case: title`
- brand: `mood.type.case: none`, `mood.type.case: sentence`, `mood.type.case: upper`, `mood.type.case: lower`, `mood.type.case: title`, `brand.case: none`, `brand.case: sentence`, `brand.case: upper`, `brand.case: lower`, `brand.case: title`
- template: `template.element.treatment: case`

Examples: yes - an eyebrow in caps; no - a title as typed.

## The schema map (maps.json)

Every enum value and string const of the five schemas + the input format + the template record (V1), by path, maps to one term or the path is
excluded with its reason (`__tests__/maps.test.js` collects the paths from the schema files, so a new name without a
map fails).

| source | paths | values -> term |
|---|---|---|
| `deck.element.type` | `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/type` | text -> E1:text; image -> E1:image; shape -> E1:shape; line -> E1:line; chart -> E1:chart; table -> E1:table; group -> E1:group |
| `deck.shape.kind` | `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/shape/properties/kind` | rect -> E4:rect; ellipse -> E4:ellipse; line -> E1:line; polygon -> E4:polygon; path -> E4:svg. a shape kind is the outline geometry it is drawn with (E4 mask outlines); a line kind is the E1 line |
| `deck.background.type` | `deck:#/properties/slides/items/properties/background/properties/type` | solid -> E4:solid; gradient -> E4:gradient; image -> E4:image-fill |
| `deck.gradient.type` | `deck:#/$defs/gradient/properties/type` | linear -> E4:linear-gradient; radial -> E4:radial-gradient |
| `deck.chart.chartType` | `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/chart/properties/chartType` | bar -> E3:chart-block; column -> E3:chart-block; stackedBar -> E3:chart-block; line -> E3:chart-block; area -> E3:chart-block; pie -> E3:chart-block; donut -> E3:chart-block; scatter -> E3:chart-block. chart types are forms of the one E3 term chart (a chart-form facet is not in V0) |
| `deck.chart.form` | `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/chart/properties/form` | funnel -> E3:chart-block; waterfall -> E3:chart-block; radar -> E3:chart-block; gauge -> E3:chart-block. chart forms are forms of the one E3 term chart |
| `deck.text.case` | `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/text/properties/font/properties/case` | none -> E4:case; upper -> E4:case; lower -> E4:case; title -> E4:case. every case value (none = as typed) is the one E4 facet case |

Excluded paths (they name no kind of thing):

- the schema id (a version string): `deck:#/properties/schema/const`, `layout:#/properties/schema/const`, `content:#/properties/schema`, `content:#/allOf/0/if/properties/schema/const`, `mood:#/properties/schema/const`, `brand:#/properties/schema/const`, `template:#/properties/schema/const`
- alignment: a parameter of a box, not a kind of thing: `deck:#/$defs/paragraph/properties/align`, `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/text/properties/align`, `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/text/properties/valign`, `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/table/properties/align/items`, `layout:#/properties/boxes/items/properties/align/properties/h`, `layout:#/properties/boxes/items/properties/align/properties/v`, `content:#/$defs/blockV1/oneOf/10/properties/align/items`, `content:#/$defs/table/properties/align/items`, `mood:#/properties/type/properties/align/properties/title`, `mood:#/properties/type/properties/align/properties/body`, `brand:#/$defs/halign`, `input:#/$defs/hAlign`, `input:#/$defs/vAlign`, `input:#/properties/layouts/items/properties/textSide`, `input:#/properties/layouts/items/properties/textPosition`, `input:#/$defs/designElement/properties/align`
- image fit (cover / contain / fill / tile): how a picture is scaled into its box, a parameter; no test on a reference can tell it without the source file: `deck:#/properties/slides/items/properties/background/properties/fit`, `deck:#/$defs/element/properties/image/properties/fit`, `brand:#/$defs/background/properties/imageFit`, `input:#/$defs/background/properties/imageFit`, `input:#/$defs/cardBlock/properties/fit`
- a report severity, not a thing on a slide: `deck:#/$defs/warning/properties/severity`, `brand:#/properties/rules/items/properties/severity`, `brand:#/properties/questions/items/properties/severity`, `input:#/properties/rules/items/properties/severity`
- a palette surface slot (which colour set a slide uses), not a thing on the slide: `layout:#/properties/surface/properties/prefer`, `mood:#/properties/palette/properties/surfaces/items/properties/role`, `input:#/properties/surfaces/items/properties/role`
- light / dark tone of a surface: a colour property: `mood:#/properties/palette/properties/surfaces/items/properties/tone`, `brand:#/properties/surfaces/items/properties/tone`
- a show / hide / size switch, not a kind of thing: `layout:#/properties/footer`, `layout:#/properties/logo`, `mood:#/properties/logo/properties/perKind/additionalProperties`, `brand:#/properties/logos/properties/perLayout/additionalProperties`, `input:#/properties/brand/properties/logoRules/properties/perLayout/additionalProperties`, `input:#/properties/layouts/items/properties/logo`
- flow direction (row / column / grid): the direction a box lays out its items, a parameter (the E3 structures column and grid are identified from the measured result): `layout:#/properties/boxes/items/properties/flow/properties/direction`
- a trend direction of a KPI value (up / down / flat), a data attribute: `content:#/$defs/blockV1/oneOf/6/properties/items/items/properties/trend`, `content:#/$defs/kpiNode/properties/trend`
- frequency is how often a thing appears, not a thing: `mood:#/properties/decor/properties/elements/items/properties/frequency`, `brand:#/properties/decor/properties/elements/items/properties/frequency`, `input:#/$defs/designElement/properties/frequency`, `input:#/$defs/gradientUse/properties/frequency`
- density / shape language / motion family / chart palette / gradient policy: a style setting of the whole brand: `mood:#/properties/geometry/properties/density`, `mood:#/properties/composition/properties/density`, `brand:#/properties/composition/properties/density`, `input:#/properties/composition/properties/density`, `mood:#/properties/shape/properties/language`, `mood:#/properties/motion/properties/family`, `mood:#/properties/charts/properties/palette`, `brand:#/properties/colors/properties/gradients/properties/policy`, `input:#/properties/gradients/properties/policy`
- a divider style (line / none / accent-bar) of the Mood: the style of the E2 divider, not another thing: `mood:#/properties/shape/properties/divider/properties/style`
- typography settings (units, font formats, styles, sources, auto-fit): `brand:#/properties/typography/properties/sizeUnits`, `input:#/properties/typography/properties/sizeUnits`, `brand:#/$defs/fontFile/properties/format`, `brand:#/$defs/fontFile/properties/style`, `input:#/$defs/font/properties/source`, `input:#/$defs/font/properties/files/items/properties/style`, `input:#/$defs/font/properties/style`, `input:#/properties/typography/properties/autoFit`, `input:#/properties/cards/properties/defaults/properties/overflow`

- **roadmap -> E3:items (items.heading-description)**: 9 (L18-3, L18-11, L18-31, L31-4, L31-12, L31-7, L31-14, L31-18, L31-13). The roadmap is labelled 01 / 1 / a region / nothing and no line joins its items: nothing visible marks a sequence (no period, no step word, no connector). The connector is measured for every container since V1 (geometry `connector`, scripts/catalogue-geometry.mjs) and decides the roadmaps whose one line crosses every labelled item (process.connector); these nine are drawn as rows (numbered, or unlabelled on L31-12) with a rule between each (7), numbered columns with no line (1) or cards with their own top rules (1), each exactly as the catalogue draws a numbered list (12 list / column-list containers are numbered alike).
- **list_with_description -> E3:compare (compare.two-sides)**: 5 (L1-2, L1-6, L2-3, L2-6, L24-5). Two items side by side with a rule between them and no numbering: drawn exactly as the catalogue draws a comparison. No visible test separates them.
- **comparison -> E3:items (items.heading-description)**: 3 (L15-9, L15-5, L15-11). A comparison drawn as two stacked items, or side by side without a rule between, or labelled with a period ("2022 to 2024"): no visible contrast mark.
- **chart -> -:unknown (none)**: 2 (L8-53, L11-6). Its bar labels mix label (6 words or fewer) and bullet (7 words or more), so no block rule holds (every field a label / every field a bullet).
- **multi_column_list -> E3:compare (compare.two-sides)**: 2 (L28-2, L28-6). As above: two columns side by side with a rule between.
- **list_with_description -> E3:process (process.connector)**: 1 (L1-35). Four numbered items in a row joined by one line between the numerals and the text: drawn exactly as a roadmap (the connector rule takes it). No visible test separates them.
- **chart -> E3:points (points.bullets)**: 1 (L7-8). The chart's figures sit in unmarked item elements outside its marked element (the block's own text is read from the marked element), so its labels show no data labels and read as bullets.

- **value -> E2:heading (heading.item)**: 9 (L4-96, L4-95, L4-134, L4-128, L4-140, L4-142, L8-35, L8-105, L37-59). The KPI value is not a number pattern: a word figure ("No findings", "Sub-second", "Elevenfold" is caught) or a bare count with two words ("6 use cases", "4 big bets": the pattern allows one word after a bare count so that "2 key findings" stays a heading). The item then leads with it as its heading.
- **body -> E2:description (description.under-heading)**: 9 (L4-96, L4-95, L4-134, L4-128, L4-140, L4-142, L8-35, L8-105, L37-59). Follows from the value miss above: with no big-number in the item, its body is the description of the (mis-read) heading.
- **heading -> E2:description (description.under-heading)**: 6 (L4-96, L4-95, L4-134, L4-140, L8-35, L8-105). Follows from the value miss above (a value + heading + body item: the value leads, the heading reads as its description).
- **point -> E2:bullet (bullet.list-line)**: 6 (L7-8, L8-53, L11-6). Two causes. L8-53 / L11-6: a bar label of 7 words or more ("US chatbot users: use it as search") fails the label test (6 words or fewer). L7-8: the chart's figures sit in unmarked item elements outside its marked element, so its block shows no data labels and its labels read as list lines.
